entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""The central government does collec..."
entries.dialogueText: "The central government does collect a flat income tax of ten percent. This is mostly paid by workers, since nobles have no income to speak of."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""I didn't make the rules, Your Maje..."
entries.dialogueText: "I didn't make the rules, Your Majesty. They were proposed by the House of Delegates and agreed on by your father."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""We definitely could, Your Majesty.""
entries.dialogueText: "We definitely could, Your Majesty."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""I do happen to think that taxing w..."
entries.dialogueText: "I do happen to think that taxing wealthy nobles makes more sense than taxing the workers who generate said wealth."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""On the other hand, the current tax..."
entries.dialogueText: "On the other hand, the current tax code was proposed by the House of Delegates and agreed on by your father. It might not be easy to change it."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Ten percent... that's low, isn't i..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ten percent... that's low, isn't it?"

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""Compared to most of our neighbors,..."
entries.dialogueText: "Compared to most of our neighbors, yes. We do provide a high standard of social services to our people, but it's mostly financed with trade income."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""This is by the House of Delegates'..."
entries.dialogueText: "This is by the House of Delegates' design, Your Majesty. Lowering the tax burden on citizens leads to higher satisfaction with the government and less likelihood of rebellion."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Actually, could we raise that rate?""
entries.dialogueText: "Actually, could we raise that rate?"

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""The commoners should consider them..."
entries.dialogueText: "The commoners should consider themselves lucky. Ten percent is far lower than elsewhere."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Nor should we. Taxing nobles would..."
entries.dialogueText: "Nor should we. Taxing nobles would be an attack on the very backbone of Rizian society."

entries.speaker: Lucita Azaro
entries.title: Lucita Azaro: ""Yes, our families' investments pow..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, our families' investments power half the businesses in this country. Why should we be forced to pay double?"

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""But nobles only got the money for..."
entries.dialogueText: "But nobles only got the money for those investments by siphoning it from hard-working commoners. Isn't it our responsibility to break the cycle somehow?"

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""You have a point. We shouldn't dis..."
entries.dialogueText: "You have a point. We shouldn't disincentivize families like yours from supporting Rizia's economy."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I'm still not convinced. But I'll..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm still not convinced. But I'll drop the subject for now."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I still think that rate could be h..."
entries.dialogueText: "I still think that rate could be higher. Imagine what we could do with the funding!"

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""A wise idea. But it leaves us at t..."
entries.dialogueText: "A wise idea. But it leaves us at the mercy of our resources and trade partners."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I understand. We certainly don't w..."
entries.dialogueText: "I understand. We certainly don't want another uprising."

entries.speaker: Lucita Azaro
entries.title: Lucita Azaro: ""And our family's investments power..."
entries.dialogueText: "And our family's investments power half of Rizia's businesses anyway. Why ask us to pay double?"

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""I don't think it would be wise. Th..."
entries.dialogueText: "I don't think it would be wise. The House of Delegates determined that lowering the tax burden on citizens leads to higher satisfaction with the government and less likelihood of rebellion."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""It's no wonder there hasn't been a..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's no wonder there hasn't been another uprising when they're paying that little."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Yes, this was the House of Delegat..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, this was the House of Delegates' intention. Lowering the tax burden on citizens leads to higher satisfaction with the government and less likelihood of rebellion."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I do wonder if the nobility should..."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""That would be a risk, Your Majesty..."
entries.dialogueText: "That would be a risk, Your Majesty. Without any other revenue-generating measure to replace that tax, it would leave us completely reliant on our natural resources."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""We already have a budget surplus,..."
entries.dialogueText: "We already have a budget surplus, Your Majesty. I see no need to raise taxes unless it's absolutely necessary."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""Not completely. But yes, if our in..."
entries.dialogueText: "Not completely. But yes, if our international trade were to be disrupted, we would have to abandon this system."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""At the moment, we have little risk..."
entries.dialogueText: "At the moment, we have little risk of that."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Hugo looked at me strangely."
entries.dialogueText: Hugo looked at me strangely.

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""It is our responsibility to make w..."
entries.dialogueText: "It is our responsibility to make wise choices with the money we have. Dwelling on how we came to have it accomplishes nothing."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Think of your own house, Your Maje..."
entries.dialogueText: "Think of your own house, Your Majesty. Would the Rizian wine industry be where it is without our backing?"

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""Very well, Your Majesty. For the r..."
entries.dialogueText: "Very well, Your Majesty. For the record, I'm not convinced either."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""In terms of our provinces' individ..."
entries.dialogueText: "In terms of our provinces' individual contributions... they pay less than three percent directly to the Crown, which mostly goes towards administrative costs."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""Brenas is still suffering the effe..."
entries.dialogueText: "Brenas is still suffering the effects of the loss of Iza and Zille. However, it's made advances in shipping and agriculture, alongside its gold mines."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""That is a slippery slope, Mr. Esqu..."
entries.dialogueText: "That is a slippery slope, Mr. Esquibel."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""After the Wehlen Civil War, we beg..."
entries.dialogueText: "After the Wehlen Civil War, we began granting 'labor hand' visas to Wehzek migrants and a smaller number of Derdians."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""Are you familiar with Rizia's two-..."
entries.dialogueText: "Are you familiar with Rizia's two-tier employment system, Your Majesty?"

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Please explain it to me.""
entries.dialogueText: "Please explain it to me."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Yes, I believe I am.""
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, I believe I am."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""Labor hands may accept employment..."
entries.dialogueText: "Labor hands may accept employment by Rizian industries, but they don't have the right to social security or other benefits. And there is a cap on how much they are allowed to earn."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""They now make up most of our blue-..."
entries.dialogueText: "They now make up most of our blue-collar workforce, with higher-paid jobs held by native Rizians as well as smaller numbers of Lespians, Valgslandians and Rumburgians."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""The program did wonders for the ec..."
entries.dialogueText: "The program did wonders for the economy when King Valero initiated it. But as a result, we now have millions of workers in this country who are being treated like second-class citizens."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""Granting 'labor hand' visas to Weh..."
entries.dialogueText: "Granting 'labor hand' visas to Wehzeks and Derdians did wonders for our economy in the 1930s and 40s."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""But as a result, Rizia now has a m..."
entries.dialogueText: "But as a result, Rizia now has a millions-strong workforce that is essentially treated like second-class citizens."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""They should have the same working..."
entries.dialogueText: "They should have the same working rights as their Rizian counterparts. Especially if they're paying taxes."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""If the system functions, I see no..."
entries.dialogueText: "If the system functions, I see no need to change it."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Those visas were granted to tempor..."
entries.dialogueText: "Those visas were granted to temporary residents. They were supposed to go home at some point."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I see where you're going with this..."
entries.dialogueText: "I see where you're going with this, but granting them full employment rights would lead to a flood of uncontrolled migration."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Rizia offered Wehzeks asylum where..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rizia offered Wehzeks asylum where other countries did not. There must be some limit to our generosity."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""I wouldn't say it functions. Barri..."
entries.dialogueText: "I wouldn't say it functions. Barring these people from upward mobility will have consequences in the long term. The worker shortage Elena mentioned is just one of those."

entries.speaker: Elena Werner
entries.title: Elena Werner: ""That was the initial aim. But Rizi..."
entries.dialogueText: "That was the initial aim. But Rizia's current-day economy now relies on these workers."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""All the more reason why they deser..."
entries.dialogueText: "All the more reason why they deserve an upgrade in status."

entries.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
entries.title: Laurento Esquibel: ""I'm not sure about that. The situa..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm not sure about that. The situation in Wehlen has stabilized since the Civil War."
